To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intra‐ and intermolecular inter‐body interactions can be described with similar residue‐specific potentials, which are solvent‐mediated, and can be reduced into a small set of residue‐ and solvent‐mediated energy parameters.

the solvent‐mediated inter‐molecular potentials are highly correlated with the corresponding intra‐molecular ones, and that the solvent‐effect is the dominant factor controlling inter‐residue energetics.

solvent‐mediated inter‐residue interaction energies are highly similar for intra‐molecule and inter‐molecule interactions, and are highly discriminative, while residue‐mediated intermolecule interactions are less discriminative and less similar to the intramolecule counterparts.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the residue‐specific inter‐molecular residue potentials derived from interfaces are very similar to the corresponding intra‐molecular potentials, but not exactly identical.

solvent‐mediated inter‐molecular potentials, which are derived from interfacial regions, are highly correlated with those obtained from the intra‐molecular interactions within single monomers, while residue‐mediated potentials show a lower correlation.
intra‐ and intermolecular interactions are very similar in their nature and energetics, with the exception of the residue‐mediation effect, which is more significant at the inter‐molecular level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the residue‐mediation effect is not as important as previously suggested, and the solvent‐mediation effect dominates the inter‐residue interaction energy.

, while the residue‐mediation effect is important, it is secondary to the solvent‐mediation effect in controlling the effective interactions between residues, either at interfaces or within single monomer structures, and that the latter can be represented by a reduced set of 23 parameters.
solvent‐mediated residue interactions, either intra‐ or inter‐molecular, are governed by the same set of energy parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the solvent‐mediated potential is highly discriminative, which is the key to understanding the specificity of the protein‐protein interactions.
the same energy parameters are valid to represent both intra‐ and intermolecular interactions, provided that the solvent is taken into account.
the same residue‐specific inter‐residue energy parameters can be used to represent both intra‐ and intermolecular inter‐actions in protein structures.
